textbook:
Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a SINGLE Borrelia burgdorferi SPIROCHAETE bacterium, centered in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous negative space for later labels. Semi-flat vector-style shading, crisp clean boundaries, a MUTED desaturated educational palette of soft dusty tints with THIN clean outlines and gentle soft shading, on a neutral dark charcoal background. Never bright primary or cartoon colours, never heavy black cartoon strokes.

SHAPE — read this carefully, it is the whole point of the figure. The cell is a HAIR-THIN THREAD of CONSTANT SLIM WIDTH along its entire length, at least fifteen times longer than it is wide, and it UNDULATES CONTINUOUSLY FROM TIP TO TIP. It travels as a long shallow diagonal sweep from the lower left to the upper right of the frame in a LOOSE, IRREGULAR, GENTLY SERPENTINE FLAT WAVE of FIVE soft, shallow, slightly uneven undulations — like a slack wet noodle or a dropped shoelace lying flat on a table. Both tips are inside the frame.

TWO ERRORS TO AVOID ABOVE ALL:
(1) NO STRAIGHT SECTION. Not one part of the cell may be drawn as a straight rod, a straight capsule or a straight tube. The wave runs unbroken through the middle of the cell exactly as it does at the ends.
(2) NO BULGE. The thread must never widen, swell, balloon, or fatten anywhere — no spindle, no almond, no leaf, no lens, no pod, no worm, no banana, no caterpillar belly in the middle. It is the same slim width everywhere, tapering only very slightly at the two tips.

CUTAWAY: the pale blue-grey OUTER MEMBRANE (outer sheath), delicately studded with small dusty-rose surface lipoprotein knobs, sleeves the whole cell. Along the upper side of the thread it is peeled back in a long, narrow, soft-edged ribbon-shaped window that FOLLOWS THE CURVE OF THE WAVE for most of the cell's length — the window is a curved sliver hugging the wave, never a straight rectangle, never a capsule, and it does NOT widen the cell. Through it the interior shows: the pale straw-coloured PERIPLASMIC SPACE, and lying in it, wrapping the inner protoplasmic cylinder as a flat ribbon and running lengthwise along the whole wave, about eight slender coral-pink PERIPLASMIC FLAGELLA, plainly SEALED INSIDE the sheath. Each bundle ends at a small deep-rust rotary motor set a little short of a pole; the two bundles overlap near mid-cell. Beneath them a thin sage-green peptidoglycan cell wall over a muted violet inner plasma membrane; inside, a pale sand cytoplasm carrying a dusty blue-purple STRAIGHT LINEAR chromosome thread drawn out lengthwise along the wave, a few tiny sage-green plasmids (short straight rods and minute rings) and numerous tiny scattered teal ribosome dots.

THE SILHOUETTE IS A SINGLE CLOSED UNBROKEN RIBBON. Nothing whatsoever emerges from the cell: both tips are smooth, bare and blunt, and no whip, tail, thread, hair, loop, streamer or line of any kind leaves its outline anywhere. This organism's flagella are INTERNAL and stay completely hidden inside it.

Do NOT draw a capsule or halo, no shaggy LPS or O-antigen fringe, no mesosome, no circular DNA loop, no membrane-bound organelles, no straight rod, no stubby cell, and no ticks, grass, skin or scene props. Anatomically faithful, single specimen only. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks, and fill the whole square edge-to-edge with no border, frame, vignette or letterbox.

It must read like a slack thread or wet noodle resting on a surface, NOT a tight coiled spring, NOT a rigid corkscrew, NOT a short curved comma rod.
